lines: Show them, right in the thread. This is photos in chat.
In the composer, choose Photo, then pick one on your device, or take one.
It waits above the message field, with Remove photo, until you send it.
Send it with text, or without. In the thread, a photo is at most sixteen rem wide, at four by three, with any text under it.
A file over ten megabytes is refused, and says why: This file is fourteen megabytes. Photos can be up to ten.
So is one that isn't a JPEG, PNG, WebP or HEIC photo. Dismiss puts it away.
And a photo someone else sends arrives as it's sent. Here is Walt's, with no reload.
Choose a photo, and it opens full screen.
Sent in Everyone, it is in Photos too, under the sender's name. From ten twenty-four pixels, a side panel says who, and when.
In a direct message, it works the same way, but it stays between the two of you: not in Photos, and only you two can open it.

lines.text: On a phone, the thread fills the screen.
As it grows, the rail, the conversations and who is here now open beside it.

lines: Once the Popkin wraps up, its photos stay, and still open. There is no Photo to send another.
What no screen shows: location and device data are removed before a photo is stored, and its address is signed, and expires.
The server checks the file's own bytes, whatever its name says. And once a photo is up, a message tried again doesn't upload it twice.
That is journey thirteen. Popkin is a free platform for pop-up communities.
